title: Charge API quota in one place

blocks.text: Tenants of a search API pay for requests in quota units: a search costs 1, an export 5, and a bulk request whatever the pricing service quotes for its rows. Until now each endpoint charged the tenant itself, by reading `remaining(tenant)` and writing the new count back with `reset(...)`, inside `synchronized (quota)`. The bulk endpoint, written last, did the same without the `synchronized` block. Last month a tenant with 10,000 units made requests worth about 13,000.

Finish the `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Quota.java`: `tryConsume(...)` and the three endpoints of `Quota.Api`. When you're done, no charge is lost, whatever a concurrent search, export, bulk request or refund does to the same tenant at the same moment, and a request the tenant can't afford is refused without charging anything. About ten lines in total.
The tests stop one request partway, at a point of their choosing, and run another against the same tenant before letting the first go on.

cases.says: a search charges one unit and an export five
a bulk request charges the units the pricing service asks for
a request that costs more than the tenant has left is refused and charges nothing
an export that arrives while a search is charging the same tenant is not overwritten by the search
a search charged while a bulk request waits for its price is not overwritten by the bulk charge
a refund that arrives while a search is charging the same tenant is kept

origin.section: The Compound Action Belongs in the Class That Owns the Lock

concepts: Moving the compound action into the class that owns the lock, as one synchronized method, leaves no lock for a caller to forget.
When each caller locks around a compound action on a shared object, one caller that forgets the lock can overwrite the others' updates, locked callers included.
Every method of the class that touches the guarded state takes the same lock; a second lock inside the class lets updates under the other one be lost.
